巴林周日发布了两份潜在威胁警报，这是自去年 9 月以来首次发出此类警告，伊朗表示，由于美伊旨在结束近 9 个月战争的协议存在不确定性，因此袭击了位于海湾国家的美国基地。
据伊朗法尔斯通讯社报道，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队表示，他们袭击了巴林的一个美国军事基地，以报复“美国的敌对行动”。
当地时间凌晨 4 点左右可以听到爆炸声，居民报告早上 6 点 30 分左右发生了第二轮爆炸。
据伊朗国营新闻电视台报道，革命卫队表示，他们已发射六架无人机，瞄准巴林 Al-Rifaa 直升机基地的美国防空雷达。美国或巴林当局没有立即证实这一消息。
巴林是美国海军第五舰队的所在地，巴林内政部表示，敦促公民和居民保持冷静，前往最近的安全地点。它没有提供有关威胁的更多细节。
两天前，革命卫队表示，他们袭击了位于巴林的美国预警雷达。美国军方否认了这一说法，称其拦截了两架伊朗无人机，没有造成任何损坏。
结束冲突的外交努力尚未取得突破，尽管华盛顿和德黑兰推迟了战争中的直接攻击，这场战争始于2月28日美国和以色列对伊朗的袭击，随后蔓延到整个地区，德黑兰向海湾国家的美国基地发射导弹和无人机袭击。
唐纳德·特朗普总统最近几天表示，如果美国不再面临来自德黑兰或伊朗支持的也门胡塞武装的新挑衅，他可能会推迟攻击伊朗，但他将维持美国的海上封锁。
然而，在另一条战线上，胡塞武装和沙特领导的打击他们的联盟继续相互攻击，该联盟周日表示，它拦截了两枚胡塞武装向沙特首都利雅得发射的弹道导弹，并在沙特石油资源丰富的东部省拦截了三架无人机。

summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《国防一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . 日本将在AZEC峰会上提议亚洲版IEA - 日本时报
日本将在AZEC峰会上提议亚洲版IEA
日本首相高市早苗计划在建立亚洲版国际能源署（IEA）方面发挥作用，以帮助成员国分享石油储备方面的专业知识。 |泳池/通过彭博社

知情人士周日称，日本首相高市早苗计划在即将于马尼拉举行的区域峰会上提议建立亚洲版的国际能源署（IEA）。
通过设想的框架，日本旨在加强石油储备方面的合作，以应对能源危机，该框架的目的是加强亚洲能源供应链，该供应链的脆弱性在中东持续动荡后已暴露无遗。
消息人士称，高市将于周二在由 11 个成员国组成的亚洲零排放共同体 (AZEC) 峰会上介绍该计划，该共同体是一个实现碳中和的区域合作框架。
日本将在建立亚洲版IEA中发挥作用，而总部位于雅加达的东盟和东亚经济研究所（ERIA）将作为新框架的秘书处，该研究所负责调查和研究该地区的能源安全问题。
新的区域框架将与总部位于巴黎的国际能源署在东京设立的新基地合作，帮助成员国分享石油储存方面的专业知识，并制定紧急情况下释放和共享石油储备的规则。
IEA成立于1974年，第一次石油危机后，要求成员国储存相当于90天消耗量的石油。
为应对中东紧张局势，今年3月及以后IEA成员国联合大规模释放石油储备。但没有任何东盟成员国参与这一协调一致的倡议。
4月份，依赖东盟国家供应外科手套等石油产品的日本宣布启动亚洲广泛能源和资源弹性伙伴关系（Powerr Asia），旨在帮助该地区的供应链保持弹性。
在AZEC峰会的其他地方，预计高一将提议使用日本闲置的储油罐。具体来说，日本将考虑与菲律宾主导的一项倡议合作，建立东南亚联合石油储备系统，并建立允许该地区国家在紧急情况下优先购买石油的机制。
除日本和菲律宾外，AZEC成员有澳大利亚、文莱、柬埔寨、印度尼西亚、老挝、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和越南。

Japan to propose Asian version of IEA at AZEC summit
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to play a role in establishing an Asian version of the International Energy Agency (IEA) to help member nations share expertise on oil stockpiling. | POOL / VIA BLOOMBERG

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to propose at an upcoming regional summit in Manila the creation of an Asian version of the International Energy Agency (IEA), informed sources said Sunday.
Through the envisioned framework, which would call for cooperation in oil stockpiling in preparation for energy crises, Japan aims to strengthen Asia’s energy supply chains, whose vulnerability has been exposed in the wake of the ongoing Middle East turmoil.
Takaichi will present the plan at a summit Tuesday of the 11-member Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC), a regional cooperation framework for realizing carbon neutrality, the sources said.
Japan will play a role in establishing the Asian version of the IEA while the Jakarta-based Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia, or ERIA, which investigates and researches energy security issues in the region, will serve as the secretariat for the new framework.
Working with the Paris-based IEA’s new base to be set up in Tokyo, the new regional framework will help member nations share expertise on oil stockpiling and make rules on the release and sharing of oil reserves in the event of an emergency.
The IEA, established in 1974, after the first oil crisis, requires member countries to stockpile oil equivalent to 90 days of consumption.
In response to the Middle East tensions, IEA member countries jointly released oil reserves on a large scale in and after March this year. But no ASEAN member nations participated in the concerted initiative.
In April, Japan, which relies on ASEAN countries for the supply of oil-based products such as surgical gloves, announced the launch of the Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia, or Powerr Asia, which is designed to help make the region’s supply chains resilient.
Elsewhere at the AZEC summit, Takaichi is expected to propose the use of idled oil storage tanks in Japan. Specifically, Japan will consider cooperating for a Philippines-led initiative to develop a joint oil reserve system for Southeast Asia and establishing a mechanism allowing nations in the region to buy oil on a priority base in the event of an emergency.
The AZEC members other than Japan and the Philippines are Australia, Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

菲律宾与澳大利亚签署防务协议 关注中国

11月15日，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞和菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗在马尼拉出席防务协议签字仪式。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 15 日 12:49
更新于 2026 年 11 月 15 日 09:40
马尼拉 — — 菲律宾和澳大利亚于 11 月 15 日签署了一项国防合作安排，马尼拉表示，随着两国进一步深化安全关系，该安排将降低联合军事活动的官僚障碍。
菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗表示，这一安排将通过简化协调程序来简化双边访问部队地位协议（SOVFA）的实施。特奥多罗表示：“做一件事不再需要 100 个步骤，而现在只需要 10 个步骤。”他将这笔交易描述为“反繁文缛节措施”。
他表示，这一安排将为海上、空中和陆地部队以及人道主义和灾难应对方面更密切的合作铺平道路，并将加强菲律宾在包括南海在内的“可信威慑态势”。
中国国防部和外交部没有立即回应 11 月 15 日发出的置评请求。
菲律宾一直在扩大其安全关系网络，同时补充其与其条约伙伴美国的长期联盟，以应对其所称的中国在南海的侵略行为，各国在南海存在重叠的海洋主张。
澳大利亚一贯支持马尼拉在战略航道上的立场，支持国际仲裁庭 2016 年的裁决，即中国的全面主张在国际法上没有依据，但北京拒绝了这一裁决。北京坚称其在南海的行动合法且专业。它一贯反对马尼拉与其盟国进行联合军事活动，称此类演习加剧了该地区的紧张局势。
澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯正在马尼拉出席东南亚国家联盟峰会，并见证了防务协定的签署。他表示，该协议将增强海上意识和信息共享，并加强战略对话、培训、互操作性和国防基础设施发展。
Albanese 宣布澳大利亚在海域意识方面进行额外投资，包括无人机技术、设备和培训，旨在改善对海上和网络安全威胁的检测。路透社

Published Nov 15, 2026, 12:49 PM

MANILA – The Philippines and Australia signed a defence cooperation arrangement on Nov 15 that Manila said would lower bureaucratic hurdles to joint military activities, as the two countries further deepen security ties.
Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the arrangement would streamline implementation of the bilateral Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA) by simplifying coordination procedures. “Rather than 100 steps to do a single thing, it will just now take 10,” Teodoro said, describing the deal as an “anti-red tape measure”.
He said the arrangement would pave the way for closer cooperation involving maritime, air and land forces, as well as humanitarian and disaster response, and would bolster the Philippines’ “credible deterrence posture” including in the South China Sea.
China’s defence and foreign ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment sent on Nov 15.
The Philippines has been broadening its network of security ties while complementing a longstanding alliance with its treaty partner, the United States, in the face of what it describes as China’s aggressive behaviour in the South China Sea, where countries have overlapping maritime claims.
Australia has consistently supported Manila’s position on the strategic waterway, backing a 2016 ruling by an international arbitral tribunal that China’s sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision Beijing rejects. Beijing maintains that its actions in the South China Sea have been lawful and professional. It routinely opposes Manila’s joint military activities with its allied partners, saying such drills heighten tensions in the region.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese witnessed the signing of the defence pact in Manila, where he is attending a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. He said the agreement would enhance maritime awareness and information sharing and increase strategic dialogue, training, interoperability and defence infrastructure development.

content:
中国湖新落成的 300 加仑能量混合器预计到 2027 年 6 月达到生产能力，与行业合作伙伴一起为 WDU-36/B 战斧弹头建立另一个美国海军运营的来源。 NAWCWD 新闻稿 一年前，海军空战中心武器部门的能量学团队从博物馆中取出了一个战斧弹头盒。该团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合在一起，并将其装入海军武器中。他们清理了箱子。他们将PBXN-107炸药混合并填充到WDU-36/B弹头中。测试、成像和 X 射线证实团队正确填充了它。今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七颗首枚战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能源处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。这些子弹是由一台 150 加仑的 China Lake 搅拌机生产的，该搅拌机已经运行了数十年。 11 月 9 日，NAWCWD 在重建的汽车装配厂内为一台新的 300 加仑搅拌机剪彩。一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使团队达到生产率。目标是在雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保战斧式弹头持续、准时地交付给舰队。 NAWCWD 战斧技术项目办公室主任帕特里夏·霍托（Patricia Hottowe）表示，“战斧”可以让舰艇和潜艇从安全水域、远离敌人射程的地方开火。
霍托维说：“为同等或接近同等的对手储备足够的武器对国家国防至关重要。”8月份，海军授予雷神公司一份价值229亿美元的合同，以加速战斧生产。推进和能量部门负责人瑞安·亨特表示，更快的生产需要更大的弹头容量。中国湖的海军实验室和马里兰州海军水面作战中心印度司令部表示他们可以完成这项工作。但关键零件和材料可能需要长达一年的时间才能到达。在演示构建过程中，团队还发现弹头规格需要进行重大更新。 Hottowe 表示，该团队在过去一年中花了很多时间更新规范和批准的供应商名单。海军弹头技术主管部门必须批准每个新供应商。每个未来的生产商，无论是海军还是工业界，都必须按照该规范进行生产。 NAWCWD 还在签订多年合同之前购买了长周期材料。这样可以更快地提供材料。霍托维表示，该团队在日常工作的同时承担了这项工作，到目前为止几乎没有增加人员。这种情况正在改变。十多名新员工正在加入该团队。戈德特表示，他们将在经验丰富的技术人员的指导下接受大约一年的安全、质量和程序培训，然后再自行工作。戈德特说，装载弹头是最简单的部分。购买材料、招募人员和获得答案都更加困难。亨特表示，挑战来自于为固定的多年时间表而构建的系统。
现在，该系统必须在更短的时钟下运行得更快。NAWCWD 执行董事丹·卡雷尼奥 (Dan Carreño) 经常用一句话来总结这个问题：“武器需要太长时间，成本太高，而且到达目的地后就无关紧要了。”化学反应取决于数十年的实践。自 20 世纪 90 年代中期以来，该部门一直为海军空射导弹 SLAM-ER 填充弹头。戈德特说，他的团队通常会在短时间内制作出独一无二的原型。这段经历让团队在“战斧”上行动得更快。雷神公司作为主承包商建造战斧。通用动力军械和战术系统机器 t

A newly inaugurated 300-gallon energetics mixer at China Lake is slated to reach production rate by June 2027, establishing an additional U.S. Navy-run source for WDU-36/B Tomahawk warheads alongside industry partners. NAWCWD press release A year ago, the energetics team at Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. They cleaned the case. They mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. This fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. Those rounds came off a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades. On Nov. 9, NAWCWD cut the ribbon on a new 300-gallon mixer in the rebuilt Motor Assembly Compound. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let the team reach production rate. The goal is warheads ready before Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said Tomahawk lets ships and submarines fire from safe waters, out of an enemy’s range. “Having an adequate stockpile of those for a peer or near-peer adversary is critical to the nation’s defense,” Hottowe said. In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production. Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work. But key parts and materials can take up to a year to arrive. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Hottowe said the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier. Every future producer, Navy or industry, must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multiyear contract. That puts material on hand sooner. Hottowe said the team took on the work alongside its day jobs, with little added staff so far. That is changing. More than a dozen new hires are joining the team. Goedert said they will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. Goedert said loading the warhead is the easiest part. Buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Hunter said the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multiyear schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. NAWCWD Executive Director Dan Carreño often sums up the problem in one line: “Weapons take too long, cost too much, and are irrelevant when they get there.” The chemistry rests on decades of practice. The branch has filled warheads for SLAM-ER, a Navy air-launched missile, since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience let the team move faster on Tomahawk. Raytheon builds Tomahawk as the prime contractor. General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases. L3Harris loads them with explosive today. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. (U.S. Navy photo by Michael L. Smith) Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting. He said the first-article warheads lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.” In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multiyear public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. Carreño called China Lake’s energetics operation a pilot plant that will keep doing developmental testing. When industry needs NAWCWD, he said, the command now has “the legs and the horsepower to go augment.” Inside NAWCWD, the warhead effort tied the Tomahawk Technical Project Office tightly to the energetics team. Hunter said he has never seen a closer partnership in his career. China Lake’s plant layout adds speed. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” Hunter said. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild. The July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April 2022. The Nov. 9 ceremony celebrated the trio. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. The new mixer, built by B&P Littleford, works much like a kitchen stand mixer, Goedert said. It is built for thick propellants and explosives. The mixer’s bowl will weigh close to 20,000 pounds. Today, crews mix in one building and cast in another, about half a mile away. In the compound’s large mix bay, the bowl will move across the room into a lift. An hourlong move will drop to 15 minutes. Those minutes count. Once mixed, these explosives start to set. Depending on the mix, crews have a couple of hours to eight or nine hours to cast it. The new layout will give back about 45 minutes of that window. Even the lift is a China Lake design. Before the team had one, workers hoisted the 150-gallon mixer’s 4,000-pound bowl and worked beneath the suspended load. Eric Wooding, a mechanical engineer, helped design a lift for that bowl years ago. “It was an idea of some people here and nobody would bid it. So we just decided to do it ourselves,” Wooding said. China Lake’s machine shop built the frame and parts. The lift worked from the start and has stayed in regular service since 2020. When the 300-gallon mixer went in, the team told the vendor to base the larger lift’s design on that concept. Hunter said the team is ready to “stand in the gap” when the Navy calls. “When we successfully complete this warhead production and ultimately return it to industry, where production belongs,” Hunter said, “we’ll be ready to take on the next challenge.” The post U.S. Navy Expands Tomahawk Warhead Production Capacity at China Lake appeared first on Naval News .

出于安全考虑，北京实施无人机所有权禁令
10月26日，一面中国国旗在北京中央商务区的摩天大楼前飘扬。路透社

北京——北京禁止拥有无人机的禁令于周日生效，当局称这项措施将有助于确保中国首都的安全。
该禁令适用于该市面积约 16,400 平方公里（大约是比利时面积一半）的城市化和农村地区。
北京于九月宣布的这项禁令禁止拥有和储存无人驾驶飞行器（UAV），以“维护首都安全”。
还禁止将无人机或其组件运输到城市。
在周日实施之前，业主被迫扔掉他们的设备，要么在批准的回购点或在网上转售。
他们也可以将他们运送到执法区域之外。
北京是中国中央政府、最高领导人和执政的中国共产党总部的所在地，面临着严格的安全措施。
6 月份，一架小型飞机撞向该市最高的摩天大楼，造成飞行员死亡、另有 13 人受伤，引发了空域安全担忧，随后出台了这项禁令。
北京已于 2026 年 5 月禁止无人机销售，业主被要求向当局注册其设备，但可以保留它们。
现在，任何拥有无人机的人都可能面临罚款并没收其设备。
出于反恐、执法、紧急救援、农业或科学研究等特定原因，可能会给予无人机飞行豁免。
近年来，无人机在中国变得非常流行，特别是在拍摄风景方面。

Drone ownership ban comes into force in Beijing over security concerns
A Chinese national flag flies in front of skyscrapers of Beijing's Central Business District on Oct. 26. | REUTERS

Beijing – Beijing’s ban on possessing drones came into force Sunday, a measure authorities said will help ensure the security of China’s capital city.
The ban applies to both urbanized and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometers — an area roughly half the size of Belgium.
The ban, which Beijing announced in September, outlaws owning and storing uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) to “safeguard the security of the capital.”
Transporting drones or their components into the city was also forbidden.
Owners had been forced to get rid of their devices ahead of Sunday’s implementation, either by reselling them at approved buy-back points or online.
They could also have transported them outside the enforcement area.
Beijing, home to China’s central government, top leaders and the headquarters of the ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP), has faced strict security measures.
The ban comes after airspace safety fears were raised in June when a small plane crashed into the city’s tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
Beijing had already banned drone sales in May 2026, with owners required to register their devices with authorities but permitted to keep them.
Now, anyone in possession of a drone could face a fine and the confiscation of their equipment.
Exemptions for drone flights may be granted for specific reasons such as counterterrorism, law enforcement, emergency relief, agriculture or scientific research.
Drones have become extremely popular in China in recent years, particularly for filming landscapes.

In a series of talks at the Navy Submarine League’s 2026 Annual Symposium, Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh (Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet – COMSUBPAC) spoke on the state o f adversary developments and activities in the Pacific, highlighting the critical threats facing the U.S. Navy’s submarine fleet. PLAN Submarines The new Type 09IIIB SSN, edited image shared on Chinese social media. RADM Cavanaugh reaffirmed the People’s Republic of China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) position as the top threat in the Indo-Pacific region when considering challenges to America’s undersea dominance, representing the one of most innovative forces facing down the U.S. Navy. However, in this instance, the Cavanaugh shed greater light on the reasoning behind China’s appraisal as the primary adversary in the undersea domain. A large element of China’s threat picture stems from the sheer rate at which the PLAN is able to put hulls in the water, with 8 Type 093B (Shang III) type Nuclear Fast Attack Submarines (SSNs) entering service in under 4 years. RADM Cavanaugh also gave credence to U.S. assessments regarding Chinese SSN production, which stipulate that a similar rate of production is sustainable by PLAN yards for at least a decade, with 20-40 Shang III or improved SSNs potentially reaching service in that timeframe. Cavanaugh further stated that the Shang III represents a serious qualitative improvement over previous Chinese SSNs, featuring advanced quieting techniques, a Vertical Launch Cell bank of 24 cells, and significant changes to the propulsion method. These improvements produced a qualitative jump to such an extent that the Shang IIIs could be considered an entirely new class of submarine. “It points to the idea that China is ready to iterate. They build Shang, they build Shang III, and they’re onto the next thing. And I would argue that iteration itself has a quality on its own.” – Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh, Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet. In regards to further developments, the U.S. sub force closely monitored processes surrounding the Type 095, China’s prospective nuclear guided missile submarine, pointing to its addition of X-form rudders and pump jet propulsion not as complete upsets, but as demonstrative of a tangible trend of innovation and risk absorption by the Chinese submarine force. Alongside the 095, the U.S. also follows the development of the Type 096 and Type 094 classes of nuclear ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs), representing key developments in China’s nuclear triad and second strike capability. Perhaps most critical, the U.S. sub force assessed the continual buildup of supporting infrastructure needed to build out and support an increasingly large and qualitatively advanced Chinese nuclear fleet. Cavanaugh also noted improvements in doctrine match any build outs of supporting infrastructure and the fleet itself, with the Chinese continually improving in their usage of nuclear submarines at a strategic and tactical level. Other PLAN Activities Chinese Research vessel Dong Fang Hong 3 docked in Qingdao. Cnsphoto via REUTERS. Following his assessment of the PLAN submarine threat, RADM Cavanaugh further highlighted PLAN efforts to better prepare its undersea force for any potential conflict, with oceanographic research, surveying, and mapping playing a large part of this component in PLAN preparations for any potential conflict with the United States or its allies. In particular, Cavanaugh confirmed a Reuters report which detailed Chinese undersea research efforts dedicated in part to mapping key operational areas near the Philippines, Taiwan, Guam, and Hawaii, including ingress and egress routes near large submarine bases in the latter two locations. Whilst these mapping efforts and the Chinese-linked vessels conducting them possess valid scientific rationale for their presence under international law, the Navy assesses this research as a vital step in preparing any undersea battlefield. Combined with increased Chinese investments across the board in Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs), their support ships, and other submersibles, the Navy assesses the Chinese approach to be more holistic in nature, identifying, laying out, and executing key steps in an organized manner to improve the sub-sea force in all aspects. The U.S. Navy assesses that all of these steps, including mapping efforts, expansion of the Chinese submarine industrial base, and continual iteration coalesce into a methodical approach designed to eventually level the playing field in the undersea domain. Russian Efforts Kazan, the first Russian Project 885M Yasen-M-class SSGN, now under operation by Russia’s Pacific Fleet. Russian MOD picture. After the PLAN, Cavanaugh highlighted Russia as the next key adversary facing America under the Pacific’s waves, presenting a somewhat different threat profile. At the top of the list includes Russia’s continual investment into its at-sea strategic deterrent, presenting mostly in the form of newer Project 955 Borei-class (also known as the Yury Dolgorukiy-class) of SSBNs, with both baseline Project 955 and newer Project 955A standard boats under Russian Pacific Fleet operation. “If you saw a graph of undersea defense threats, they’re growing rapidly. I’m talking about SSGNs, SSBNs, with Russia and China combined. And so that has significant implications for our ability to maintain domain awareness with our own force structure.” – Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh, Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet. Cavanaugh also briefly highlighted another leg of Russia’s undersea strategic deterrent in the Poseidon nuclear XLUUV (also known as Status-6) as an unconventional threat profile that the U.S. Pacific submarine force would have to grapple with. Amongst the slides, alluded to was the threat presented by Russia’s Yasen or Severodvinsk-class of SSGNs, presenting an extremely quiet class of boats capable of carrying dozens of hypersonic or cruise missiles within close proximity to the U.S.’s coast. Combined with continued and dedicated Russian undersea efforts, Cavanaugh stressed that Russia’s consolidation of newer sea-based nuclear deterrents and continued investments into its submarine fleet still makes it a potent threat, especially when considered in conjunction with the Chinese fleet. Additionally, even as the Russian surface fleet continues to succumb to aging vessels and budget constraints, the Russian sub force will likely remain an important consideration for the threats facing U.S. undersea dominance. Last but Not Least: North Korea Image of the new North Korean SSBN during an inspection conducted by North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un. Image taken from a North Korean State Media Broadcast. North Korea’s threat profile came at the tail end of Cavanaugh’s remarks on the threats facing the U.S. submarine force and sub-sea efforts. Whilst North Korean advancements were of note, in the eyes of the U.S. Navy and its top brass, the substance backing Pyongyang’s claims remains to be seen. Despite this, any potential North Korean advancements list as increasingly consequential, especially considering the domain of at-sea nuclear capabilities. The recently revealed North Korean SSBN as well as suspected claims of advancement in torpedo and propulsion technology depict the main subjects noted in Cavanaugh’s remarks. Whilst the U.S. Navy currently withholds any final judgements on validity of the claims surrounding North Korean improvement, Cavanaugh noted that these developments represent part of an increasingly dense under-sea threat environment coming from three different countries, each with their own intricacies. title: China Lifts The Veil On Its GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon Stealth UCAV
zh_title: 中国揭开GJ-11神秘龙隐形无人机的面纱
summary: 中国为我们提供了迄今为止最清晰的 GJ-11 隐形无人战斗机 (UCAV) 展示，新的官方镜头揭示了这款飞翼无人机以前未见过的细节，包括其内部武器舱、起落架、安装在机头的传感器以及独特的排气装置。与此同时，中国人民解放军空军 (PLAAF) 还声称，GJ-11 已经完成了首次实弹打击任务，取得了成功。这有点令人费解，因为无人战斗机已经进行了多年的测试架次，包括在前方
content:
中国为我们提供了迄今为止最清晰的 GJ-11 隐形无人战斗机 (UCAV) 展示，新的官方镜头揭示了这款飞翼无人机以前未见过的细节，包括其内部武器舱、起落架、安装在机头的传感器以及独特的排气装置。与此同时，中国人民解放军空军 (PLAAF) 还声称，GJ-11 已经完成了首次实弹打击任务，取得了成功。这有点令人费解，因为无人作战飞机多年来已经进行了多次测试，包括在前沿作战地点，而且在此之前几乎无法想象是否进行过实弹武器投送。也许这是在转换过程中丢失某些东西的情况，例如使用新的内部传感器或新型武器发射。跑道上 GJ-11 的正面视图。 PLA screencap 这段视频昨天由中国国家电视台中央电视台播出，距离中国人民解放军空军成立 77 周年还有两天。随附的报告提供了有关该飞机预期任务集的更多详细信息，包括空袭和压制敌方防空系统（SEAD），以及它与有人战斗机的有人与无人编队（MUM-T）行动的整合。
新披露的信息让公众对 GJ-11 的配置有了最全面的了解，并进一步了解中国打算如何使用这款名为“玄龙”的隐形飞翼飞机。GJ-11 起飞。 PLA screencap 仔细观察 GJ-11 最暴露的视图之一显示了 GJ-11 的底面，清楚地暴露了其两个内部武器舱。腹侧舱位于飞机的混合翼体内，具有独立的门组，具有独特的锯齿状边缘——这是低可观察性飞机的常见特征。舱室的内部布局和尺寸仍不清楚，飞机可容纳的武器的精确范围也不清楚。然而，每个舱室似乎可以容纳至少 1,000 磅级武器，甚至可能容纳 2,000 磅级武器。 #GTMilitaryWatch 央视新闻军事频道周一发布了新镜头，以多角度特写镜头展示了中国人民解放军 (PLA) 空军的 GJ-11 隐形无人机。它还透露，空军首批自行训练的两架女无人机… pic.twitter.com/PPVmws9DJJ —《环球时报》（@globaltimesnews）2026年11月9日 据央视报道，这两个舱可携带多种空对地/水面弹药。
此前，中国航空工业集团公司 (AVIC) 在 2021 年中国航展上展示的 GJ-11 模型中曾透露过武器舱配置，但新的镜头可以更好地展示实际飞机。机库中 GJ-11 的正面视图，武器舱门部分打开。 PLA screencap 内部武器架是 GJ-11 隐蔽性设计的核心，使其能够携带弹药，而不会受到与外部挂架和挂具相关的雷达信号（和空气动力学）影响。此前于 2025 年 11 月发布的视频显示，GJ-11 正在飞行，起落架仍处于伸出状态。然而，其中一个新序列显示飞机起飞，随后的侧视图和后视图捕捉到了其起落架在升空后收回的情况。起落架本身非常坚固，包括一个重型起落架

【原文 English Original】
China has provided us with the clearest look yet at its GJ-11 stealth uncrewed combat aerial vehicle (UCAV), with new official footage revealing previously unseen details of the flying-wing drone, including its internal weapons bays, landing gear, nose-mounted sensor installation, and distinctive exhaust arrangement. The release also comes alongside a claim from the People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) that the GJ-11 has completed its first live-fire strike mission, scoring a hit. This is somewhat puzzling, since the UCAV has racked up test sorties for years already, including at forward operating locations, and it seems almost inconceivable that a live weapons delivery would not have been conducted before now. Perhaps this is a case of something being lost in translation, such as the use of a new internal sensor or a new type of weapon delivery. Head-on view of a GJ-11 on the runway. PLA screencap The footage, broadcast by Chinese state television’s CCTV yesterday, comes two days ahead of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the PLAAF. Accompanying reporting provides additional details about the aircraft’s intended mission set, including airstrikes and suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), as well as its integration into manned-unmanned teaming (MUM-T) operations with crewed fighters. The new disclosures offer the most comprehensive public look yet at the GJ-11’s configuration and provide further insight into how China intends to employ the stealthy flying-wing aircraft, which is named Xuanlong — Chinese for Mystery Dragon. A GJ-11 takes off. PLA screencap A closer look at the GJ-11 One of the most revealing views shows the underside of the GJ-11, clearly exposing its two internal weapons bays. Located within the aircraft’s blended wing-body, the ventral bays have separate sets of doors with distinctive serrated edges — a common feature on low-observable aircraft. The internal arrangement and dimensions of the bays remain unclear, as does the precise range of weapons the aircraft can accommodate. However, it would appear likely that each bay can accommodate at least a 1,000-pound-class and likely a 2,000-pound-class weapon. #GTMilitaryWatch CCTV News military channel released new footage on Monday offering a close-up, multi-angle look at the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force's GJ-11 stealth drone. It also revealed that two of the Air Force's first batch of self-trained female drone… pic.twitter.com/PPVmws9DJJ — Global Times (@globaltimesnews) November 9, 2026 According to CCTV , the two bays can carry a variety of air-to-ground/surface munitions. The weapons bay configuration had previously been revealed in a model of the GJ-11 displayed by the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) at Airshow China in 2021, but the new footage provides a much better look at the actual aircraft. Head-on view of a GJ-11 in the hangar, with the weapons bay doors partially open. PLA screencap Internal weapons carriage is central to the GJ-11’s low-observable design, allowing it to carry munitions without the radar signature (and aerodynamic) penalties associated with external pylons and stores. Previous footage released in November 2025 showed the GJ-11 in flight with its landing gear remaining extended. However, one of the new sequences shows the aircraft taking off, with subsequent side and rear views capturing its landing gear retracting after liftoff. The landing gear itself is notably robust, including a heavy-duty twin-wheel nose unit. With that in mind, it may be the same landing gear as used in the GJ-21, a naval variant capable of operating from aircraft carriers and big-deck assault ships. A GJ-11 retracts its landing gear on takeoff. PLA screencap The new imagery also offers a closer look at a trapezoidal glazed fairing beneath the nose. This appears consistent with an electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensor installation. Its precise configuration and capabilities have not been disclosed, but it’s worth noting that similar-looking installations also appear on the crewed J-20 and J-35 fighters, with these systems apparently being analogous to the electro-optical targeting system, or EOTS, found on the F-35 . If the sensor on the GJ-11 works like an EOTS, it would provide the drone with precision targeting and identification, lasing, as well as a secondary infrared search-and-track emulation function. A view of a GJ-11 showing the undernose EO/IR sensor installation. PLA screencap Perhaps the most distinctive external feature remains the GJ-11’s exhaust arrangement, for what is reported to be a WS-13 turbofan engine. A close-up of the rear of the aircraft shows the flattened exhaust outlet, shielded and integrated into the upper rear portion of the flying-wing airframe. Combined with the dorsal air intake and the absence of conventional exposed engine nozzles, this configuration is intended to reduce the aircraft’s radar and infrared signatures, especially from the most critical view aspects. The GJ-11’s tailless, blended-wing configuration is by now a defining feature of low-observable UCAV designs. Close-up of the tail section of a GJ-11. PLA screencap At least some of the GJ-11s shown have an air data boom on the nose. While normally associated with early flight testing, the GJ-11 is now far beyond that. The booms could still be fitted for some envelope expansion and other flight test work, although it may also simply involve earlier footage. Airstrikes and suppression of enemy air defenses Beyond the new imagery, one of the more interesting aspects of the CCTV coverage is its description of the GJ-11’s intended operational role. The broadcaster identified airstrikes and SEAD among the aircraft’s mission sets. The latter is particularly significant, as penetrating or operating within heavily defended airspace to locate and suppress or destroy enemy air defense systems is the most dangerous mission for a crewed combat aircraft. A stealthy uncrewed aircraft could contribute to these operations by carrying precision-guided weapons into more contested areas, providing additional sensing and targeting capacity, or forcing an adversary to expend valuable air defense resources. The two internal weapons bays provide the means to carry air-to-surface munitions while retaining the aircraft’s low-observable configuration. However, we don’t know which specific weapons have been integrated, their quantities, or whether the GJ-11 can employ dedicated anti-radiation weapons for SEAD missions. Alternative SEAD/DEAD loads could include multiple Small Diameter Bomb (SDB) equivalents, including those that are networked, as we have seen in previous concept videos . Many other types of standoff weapons could also be carried, with the platform itself using onboard sensors for fixing the target or acquiring targeting information from other sources via a tactical data network. Overhead view of a GJ-11 outside the hangar. PLA screencap First live-fire strike claim According to CCTV , the GJ-11 has completed its first live-fire strike mission, with two members of the PLAAF’s initial batch of female drone operators participating in the operation. One of the operators, Shi Xiaoran, described encountering cloud cover that initially obscured the target. After circling once more, she located it and released the weapon, scoring a hit. A drone controller flies a GJ-11 from a command-and-control trailer. PLA screencap One aspect that remains unclear is the extent to which the aircraft can independently identify and engage targets. A successful strike would demonstrate weapons employment, but not necessarily autonomous targeting or engagement. A view of a GJ-11 showing its triangular engine intake and undernose sensor installation. PLA screencap Manned-unmanned teaming with J-16 and J-20 fighters Perhaps the most strategically important aspect of the new coverage is its emphasis on manned-unmanned teaming. The CCTV footage showed mission planning involving a GJ-11 operating alongside J-16 Flanker multirole fighters and, in a separate sequence, J-20 fifth-generation stealth fighters. This provides a more explicit indication of the role China envisions for the GJ-11 within its broader combat aviation ecosystem. The J-16 provides a powerful multirole platform for strike and electronic warfare-related missions , while the J-20 offers a stealthy crewed counterpart for operations in highly contested airspace. An uncrewed aircraft operating alongside either type could extend the formation’s sensor coverage, carry additional weapons, conduct reconnaissance, or undertake particularly hazardous missions. A J-16D electronic warfare aircraft. via Chinese internet As a loyal wingman, the GJ-11’s role would extend beyond simply carrying weapons, with the UCAV able to act as an additional airborne sensor and strike platform, allowing crewed aircraft to distribute tasks across a larger formation. At the same time, the footage does not establish how the UCAVs communicate with their crewed counterparts, how targeting information is shared, or the level of autonomy available to the GJ-11. The new footage shows the drone being flown under man-in-the-loop (MITL) direct control, but it likely features, or will feature, semi-autonomous control modes, especially for teaming applications, which will require a high degree of onboard autonomy. We do know that China expects the UCAV to be controlled by crewed aircraft, as part of its basic concept. The PLAAF has at least trialed crewed aircraft as drone controllers , and this is one mission set that has frequently been ascribed to the two-seat J-20S . A stock photo of the two-seat J-20S. via X From prototype to operational platform After years of development involving the experimental Sharp Sword design , the much more evolved GJ-11 platform was publicly unveiled during China’s National Day military parade in Beijing in October 2019. Its development is associated with Hongdu Aviation Industry Group, part of the broader AVIC aviation-industrial structure. Two views of an early Sharp Sword UCAV demonstrator. via X A model displayed by AVIC at Airshow China in 2021 provided an early indication of the aircraft’s internal weapons-carrying arrangement. In November 2025, as we reported at the time , the PLAAF released footage of the GJ-11 flying alongside a J-20 and a J-16D electronic warfare aircraft, suggesting that it may have entered service or was at least being integrated into the service’s broader air combat architecture. A screencap from an earlier video showing a GJ-11 flying alongside a J-16D and a J-20. PLA screencap Development and testing of the GJ-11 have been underway for years, with notable activity at China’s secretive Malan test facility in Xinjiang. Satellite imagery reviewed by TWZ has documented repeated, and at times near-daily, GJ-11 activity there, including multiple aircraft operating together. The deployment of three GJ-11s to Shigatse in Tibet between August and September 2025 provided an additional indication that the program was moving beyond test work toward operational evaluation. Two GJ-11s seen on the ramp at Malan on July 12, 2024. PHOTO © 2024 PLANET LABS INC. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. REPRINTED BY PERMISSION Another image circulating on Chinese social media shows three additional GJ-11s parked alongside another example of the same type. Three GJ-11s in a hangar. PLA screencap Another hangar view with likely a fourth GJ-11 just visible on the right. PLA screencap According to Andreas Rupprecht, an expert on Chinese aviation and contributor to TWZ , numbers that can be seen on the drones themselves likely point to these aircraft being low-rate initial production (LRIP) examples. And what’s even more interesting is that, for the first time, numbers are clearly visible which – and I’m going to go out on a limb here – I believe are not serial numbers but rather design numbers. The numbers 0003, 0011 and 0012 are visible, so these are probably LRIP aircraft. pic.twitter.com/zH2D2Narr9 — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) November 10, 2026 The new releases come less than a month after China announced that the GJ-21 naval derivative had completed its first launch and recovery aboard the new Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan , which is equipped with an electromagnetic catapult and arresting gear. The milestone would pave the way for the PLA Navy to field a shipborne stealth UCAV for strike and reconnaissance missions. However, China has yet to release actual footage of the claimed operation, leaving it independently unverified. The Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan seen leaving Hudong-Zhonghua Shipyard for its first sea trials. Government of the People’s Republic of China The broader significance of the GJ-11 lies in the fact that it’s a genuine UCAV, not simply a loyal wingman designed to accompany a crewed fighter . Free of the endurance limitations imposed by a human crew, a platform of this class could likely offer at least twice the combat radius of a comparable crewed fighter. More importantly, it is intended to have the autonomy to conduct tactical missions independently, as well as operate alongside crewed aircraft. That opens up the possibility of extending China’s strike and reconnaissance reach considerably beyond what its existing low-observable crewed combat aircraft can achieve. The GJ-11’s flying-wing configuration, internal weapons bays, and emphasis on signature reduction suggest a platform approaching the very-low-observable (VLO) category. At the same time, China is now openly fielding a capability that the United States has conspicuously failed to bring into public operational service. In the late 2000s and early 2010s, the United States appeared to be leading the way in stealth UCAV development, with programs such as the Boeing Phantom Ray , X-45 , and X-47B demonstrating the potential of autonomous, long-range penetrating aircraft. Yet those ambitions effectively disappeared from the publicly acknowledged force-development agenda. The Pentagon has instead concentrated on lower-end and less capable Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), generally designed to operate in conjunction with crewed fighters . Northrop Grumman’s X-47B UCAV demonstrator. U.S. Navy Northrop Grumman’s much larger X-47B that also featured a ‘cranked kite’ planform. USN As we argued in our earlier examinations of the American UCAV gap , the absence of a publicly acknowledged, sizeable force of independent, long-range stealth combat drones remains a significant weakness in U.S. airpower planning. Classified programs may exist, and the U.S. military certainly operates highly sophisticated stealthy uncrewed reconnaissance platforms , but even a small clandestine combat capability would be unlikely to make a decisive difference in a major, sustained conflict. China, meanwhile, is moving towards making this class of aircraft a central part of its military inventory. Important questions about the GJ-11 remain, particularly regarding its actual weapons load, various specifications, its degree of autonomy, and its ability to operate in coordination with crewed fighters. However, the latest official coverage provides the clearest indication yet of how China intends to employ its stealth UCAV in a future conflict, and sheds a little more light on the Mystery Dragon. 菲律宾与中国在南海问题上的裂痕加深海峡时报
菲律宾与中国在南海问题上的分歧加深
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
资料照片：2026 年 7 月 20 日，中国海岸警卫队和菲律宾海军舰艇在南海仁爱礁发生冲突，截取自讲义视频。杰·塔里拉（Jay Tarriela）来自 X/讲义来自 REUTERS/档案照片
发表于 2026 年 11 月 15 日 1:24
更新于 2026 年 11 月 15 日 1:24
马尼拉，11 月 15 日 - 在菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯 (Ferdinand Marcos Jr) 的领导下，马尼拉和北京之间的关系恶化，马尼拉转向支持菲律宾与中国的海上争端的美国。
以下是过去两年中导致菲律宾和中国之间紧张局势升级的关键事件的时间表：
1月6日——菲律宾部署船只和飞机在专属经济区监视中国最大的海警船。
2月18日——马尼拉指责中国海军在黄岩岛附近进行危险的飞越；北京纠纷。
3 月 28 日——卫星图像显示，中国在黄岩岛周围部署了两架轰 6 轰炸机。
5 月 5 日——菲律宾对中国科考船提出质疑，称其在伊罗戈海岸进行非法海洋调查。
8 月 4 日——菲律宾和印度海军首次在南海联合航行。
8月12日——马尼拉批评中国在黄岩岛的“危险举动”；称他们导致了中国船只相撞。
8 月 13 日——中国表示驱逐了在黄岩岛附近航行的美国驱逐舰；美国海军表示其行动符合国际法。

content:
发言人办公室关于美日海底矿产资源开发的联合声明 媒体报道 2026 年 11 月 12 日 以下声明的文本由美利坚合众国和日本政府在美国负责海底矿产开发的跨部门代表团访问日本之际发布。开始文本。美国和日本政府重申，经济安全合作是美日联盟不可或缺的一部分，安全、有弹性和多样化的关键矿产供应链对两国的繁荣和国家安全至关重要。两国政府认识到负责任的海底矿产资源开发的潜力，可以使关键矿产供应多样化、创造新的商业机会并支持两国的工业基础。这项合作建立在特朗普总统和高市首相于 2025 年 10 月签署的《美日通过采矿和加工确保关键矿产和稀土供应的框架》中规定的共同目标的基础上，并通过美日双边举措得到推进，其中包括美国商务部与日本经济产业省于 2026 年 3 月签署的合作备忘录 (MoC)。
两国政府对谅解备忘录所取得的进展表示欢迎，包括 11 月 11 日至 12 日在日本富山举行的美日工作组第二次会议，会议讨论了日本南鸟岛附近的稀土泥浆项目及其多金属结核项目，以及扩大了政府官员、行业利益相关者、研究人员和技术专家之间的接触。展望未来，美国和日本政府计划推进以下优先事项： 深化与美国和日本的接触行业利益相关者并在整个海底矿物供应链中建立值得信赖的商业伙伴关系；确保值得信赖的合作伙伴之间的处理能力，以减少供应链漏洞；保护敏感技术和专有信息；交流与深海勘探、海底测绘和资源表征、环境评估、缓解和监测、技术创新和资源开发相关的先进技术和方法的信息和最佳实践；探索促进科学理解的机会，例如协调船只、自主水下航行器和其他相关资产的访问和使用，以支持联合研究、技术演示和各自的美国项目。

Office of the Spokesman Joint Statement on U.S.-Japan Seabed Mineral Resource Development Media Note November 12, 2026 The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Japan on the occasion of a visit to Japan by a U.S. interagency delegation focused on seabed minerals development. Begin Text. The Governments of the United States and Japan reaffirm that economic security cooperation is an indispensable part of the U.S.-Japan Alliance and that secure, resilient, and diversified critical mineral supply chains are essential to the prosperity and national security of both countries. The two governments recognize the potential for responsible seabed mineral resource development to diversify critical mineral supplies, create new commercial opportunities, and support the two countries’ industrial bases. This cooperation builds on the shared objectives set out in the United States-Japan Framework for Securing the Supply of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths through Mining and Processing, signed by President Trump and Prime Minister Takaichi in October 2025, and is being advanced through U.S.-Japan bilateral initiatives, including the Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) between the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry signed in March 2026. The two governments welcomed progress under the MoC, including the second meeting of the U.S.-Japan Working Group on November 11 and 12 in Toyama, Japan, which included discussions on Japan’s rare-earth mud project near Minamitorishima Island and its polymetallic nodules project, as well as expanded engagement among government officials, industry stakeholders, researchers, and technical experts. Looking ahead, the Governments of the United States and Japan plan to advance the following priorities: Deepen engagement with U.S. and Japanese industry stakeholders and foster trusted commercial partnerships across the full seabed mineral supply chain; Secure processing capacity among trusted partners to reduce supply chain vulnerabilities; Safeguard sensitive technologies and proprietary information; Exchange information and best practices on advanced technologies and methodologies related to deep-sea exploration, seabed mapping and resource characterization, environmental assessment, mitigation and monitoring, technological innovation, and resource development; Explore opportunities to advance scientific understanding such as coordinating access to, and use of, vessels, autonomous underwater vehicles, and other relevant assets in support of joint research, technology demonstrations, and respective U.S. and Japanese seabed exploration campaigns; Facilitate regulatory exchanges related to best practices, including for mitigation and monitoring, technological advancements, environmental assessments, data management, and adaptive management, consistent with national laws and policies; Promote clear, streamlined, and predictable regulatory approaches that facilitate private investment in the seabed minerals sector; Promote complementarity between domestic and international regulatory regimes to support commercial viability and long-term certainty for industry; and Seek additional partnerships to advance responsible seabed mineral resource development. The two governments reaffirm their commitment to whole-of-government coordination and practical cooperation that mobilizes their complementary scientific, technological, industrial, diplomatic, and financial strengths. They intend to support commercial opportunities, encourage private-sector investment, and foster trusted partnerships across mineral supply chains to accelerate responsible seabed mineral resource development, strengthen critical mineral security, and advance the shared economic security of the United States and Japan. End Text.

总统关于美国海军陆战队生日的致辞 搜索 选择类别 所有新闻简报和声明 所有总统行动 行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 所有简报和声明 总统行动 所有行政命令 提名和任命 总统备忘录公告情况说明书 发布评论 研究 两个半世纪以来，美国海军陆战队一直是美国精神的生动体现。凭借荣誉、勇气和对维护和推进美国利益的坚定承诺，海军陆战队一再证明，无论困难如何，他们都会响应每一个召唤并完成任何任务。在海军陆战队庆祝保护美国并击败敌人 251 周年之际，我向每一位为我们的国家战斗和牺牲的海军陆战队员致以最深切的谢意，并向他们无与伦比的英勇遗产致敬。从我们共和国诞生之日起，海军陆战队就一直捍卫美国赖以建立的自由和自由的支柱。独立战争期间，海军陆战队出海夺取拿骚港，为大陆军提供大量军需物资增援。在整个第二次世界大战期间，海军陆战队在整个太平洋战区发挥了关键作用，对于美国在关岛、瓜达尔卡纳尔岛、冲绳岛和硫磺岛的胜利至关重要。
这些令人难以置信的“魔鬼犬”在美国历史上无数次冲突的前线服役，从未失败过保护我们国内外的公民，并在我们的对手面前无所畏惧地展示了美国的威力和力量。今天，通过我们勇敢的海军陆战队的英勇无私的服务，美国变得更加安全。美国海军陆战队的爱国男女不断提醒人们美国伟大和荣耀的真正源泉。作为总统，我是我国历史上最强有力的海军陆战队倡导者。通过超级情报的进步以及对导弹防御、下一代能力和造船的投资，我们正在为我们的海军陆战队提供击败美国敌人所需的一切资源，无论他们身在何处。在我的领导下，我们的海军陆战队员也回到家乡，得到他们应得的关怀和支持。我的政府恢复了退伍军人事务部的常识，使退伍军人能够寻求自己选择的医疗保健提供者，降低退伍军人及其家人的费用，并减少有害的积压。作为总司令，我将永远不会停止为我们的海军陆战队挺身而出，维护他们作为世界上最致命的战斗力量的声誉。在座右铭“Semper Fidelis”（意为“永远忠诚”）的指引下，美国海军陆战队在我们国家和全人类的历史上留下了自己的印记。
我们海军陆战队的坚定力量证明了美国精神的力量和美国武装部队的力量。一代又一代，海军陆战队忠实地充当了美国的捍卫者，他们将在未来的几个世纪里继续作为自由的忠实捍卫者。永远Fi！关于美国海军陆战队生日的总统致辞首先出现在白宫。

From the dawn of our Republic, Marines have defended the pillars of freedom and liberty that America was founded upon.  During the Revolutionary War, Marines took to the sea to seize the port of Nassau and reinforce the Continental Army with large quantities of military supplies.  Throughout World War II, Marines played a critical role across the Pacific Theater and were essential to American victories at Guam, Guadalcanal, Okinawa, and Iwo Jima.  These incredible Devil Dogs have served on the front lines of countless conflicts throughout American history, never failed to protect our citizens at home and abroad, and fearlessly demonstrated American might and power in the face of our adversaries.  Today, America is made safer through the heroic and selfless service of our brave Marines. The patriotic men and women of the United States Marine Corps are enduring reminders of the true source of American greatness and glory.  As President, I have been the strongest advocate for our Marines in the history of our country.  Through advancements in Super Intelligence and investments in missile defense, next-generation capabilities, and shipbuilding, we are providing our Marines with every resource they need to defeat America’s enemies wherever they may be. Under my leadership, our Marines also return home to the care and support they have so rightly earned.  My Administration has restored common sense at the Department of Veterans Affairs, empowering veterans to seek the healthcare providers of their choice, lowering costs for veterans and their families, and slashing harmful backlogs.  As Commander in Chief, I will never stop standing up for our Marines and upholding their reputation as the most lethal fighting force the world has ever seen. Guided by their motto, Semper Fidelis, meaning “Always Faithful,” the United States Marines have left their mark on the history of our Nation and all of mankind.  The steadfast strength of our Marines is a testament to the power of the American Spirit and the might of the United States Armed Forces.  Generation after generation, Marines have faithfully served as champions of America, and they will carry on as faithful defenders of liberty for centuries to come.  Semper Fi!
